products.name: Manfrotto PIXI Mini Tripod (MTPIXI-B)
products.query: Manfrotto PIXI mini tripod black MTPIXI-B
products.summary: A fixed-height tabletop tripod with a push-button ball head and legs that fold into a grip. Digital Camera World leads its mini tripod guide with it and says it works for video conferencing at home.
products.renterNote: Anyone putting a light webcam, phone (with a clamp) or compact camera on a desk for calls. Key caveat: height is fixed at about 13.5 cm and the head tilts up only about 35 degrees, so it sits low and you may need books or a riser for eye level.
pros: Solid, simple build with a ball head reviewers say works well
Rated for about 1 kg, plenty for a webcam or phone
Legs fold into a grip, so it packs small and doubles as a handle
cons: No height adjustment, so the lens sits low on a desk
Ball head is stiff, tilts upward only about 35 degrees and shoots landscape only; phones need a separate clamp

specs.Head: Ball head with push-button release, about 35 degrees upward tilt
specs.Plate: 1/4 in screw mount; phone clamp sold separately

products.scoreNote: Compact, solid and trustworthy for light gear, but fixed at about 13.5 cm with limited tilt, so it scores low on working height.

praise: Solid, sturdy support for its size
Easy to adjust with a squeeze of the release, and usable as a hand grip with legs folded
complaints: Fixed 13 cm height makes it hard to raise the lens
Spring-loaded ball head release is stiff and tilt is limited to roughly 35 degrees

sources.title: Thomann: Manfrotto PIXI Mini customer reviews

products.name: Joby GorillaPod 3K Kit
products.query: Joby GorillaPod 3K Kit flexible tripod with ball head
products.badge: Best for monitor and shelf mounting
products.summary: A flexible-leg tripod with a ball head and bubble level, rated for 3 kg. Rosenberry Rooms recommends the 3K for versatility, and its legs wrap around objects, so it can clip a webcam to a monitor or sit on a shelf.
products.renterNote: Desk workers with a webcam, mirrorless camera or small mic who want to grip a monitor, shelf or lamp arm rather than just sit on the desk. Key caveat: flexible legs take longer to level and it is a tall-ish stand, so it will not put the lens at eye level on its own.
pros: Bendable legs wrap around monitor edges, shelves and rails
3 kg (6.6 lb) rating covers webcams, phones and light mirrorless cameras
Ball head with bubble level and panorama function
cons: Takes a little longer to level on flexible legs
Reviewers say it suits small cameras best, and Joby's 3K Kit has been reported discontinued at some retailers, so check the listing carefully

specs.Weight: 8.7 oz (247 g) stand alone per B&H spec table
specs.Material: Plastic (Galaxus lists it as a plastic tripod)
specs.Head: Ball head 3K with panorama function and bubble level
specs.Plate: 1/4 in-20 quick-release style ball head mount

products.scoreNote: Most flexible mounting of the three and a 3 kg rating, but plastic legs, slow leveling and a roughly 12 in height keep build and height modest.

praise: Great for a webcam you sometimes move off the monitor
Surprisingly sturdy and lightweight for travel and desk use
complaints: Takes longer to get level because of the flexible legs
Only suited to small cameras; the listing can be confused with the 1K Kit

products.name: Ulanzi MT-16 Extendable Tripod with Ball Head
products.query: Ulanzi MT-16 extendable tripod with ball head 2052
products.summary: A 170 g telescopic stand with fold-out legs, a 360-degree metal ball head and a cold shoe. Retailers say that as a tripod it works for video conferencing at a desk, and it extends from about 22 to 44 cm.
products.renterNote: Remote workers and streamers with a webcam, phone or action camera who want a bit more height than a fixed mini tripod plus a mic or light on the cold shoe. Key caveat: the vertical-mode load limit is reported as 500 g, so skip it for heavier mirrorless setups.
pros: Extends from about 22 to 44 cm for a more usable desk height
Light at 170 g with a lockable 360-degree metal ball head
Cold shoe mount for a microphone or small light
cons: Vertical mode limited to 500 g by one review, against a 1.5 kg headline rating
Head is not removable and the stand is less stable on uneven ground or when fully extended

specs.Max height (no center column): Not applicable (telescopic arm, no center column)
specs.Folded length: About 22 cm (22.5 cm on one listing)
specs.Max load: 1.5 kg (3.31 lb) listed; 500 g in vertical mode per a review
specs.Leg sections: Telescopic arm with 4 height steps, fold-out legs
specs.Leg lock: Twist/extension lock on the arm (type not confirmed by sources seen)
specs.Head: 360-degree lockable metal ball head, cold shoe

products.scoreNote: Lightest and tallest of the three for desk use, with a cheap-for-what-it-does feature set, but a 500 g vertical limit and an extending arm cap stability.

praise: Very well made and not cheap feeling
Extending pole is much stiffer than expected
complaints: Vertical-mode load limit is low (reported 500 g)
Head is fixed and not removable

sources.title: B&H: Ulanzi MT-16 Extendable Tripod with Ball Head customer reviews and questions
